- **Panic disorder:** recurrent unexpected panic attacks (sudden intense fear with racing heart, breathlessness, dizziness) plus persistent worry about further attacks or avoidance
- **Social anxiety disorder:** intense fear of being scrutinised or judged (Mohammed)
- **Specific phobias:** fear of particular objects/situations (heights, injections, animals)
- **Agoraphobia:** fear of situations where escape seems hard (crowds, public transport)

steps.title: Why anxiety persists: the avoidance cycle
steps.body:
Fear → avoidance → relief → avoidance is **negatively reinforced** → no chance to learn the situation is survivable → fear stays.

This is Mowrer's **two-factor theory**: fear is learned by classical conditioning and maintained by operant avoidance. It explains why **exposure** (gradual, planned facing of feared situations, without safety behaviours) is one of the most effective treatments.

steps.title: Trauma- and stressor-related disorders
steps.body:
**PTSD** can follow exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury or sexual violence. Symptom clusters (DSM-5-TR):
- **Intrusions:** flashbacks, nightmares, distressing memories
- **Avoidance** of reminders
- **Negative changes in thoughts and mood:** blame, detachment, persistent negative emotions
- **Arousal and reactivity:** hypervigilance, startle, irritability, sleep problems

Duration: **more than one month**. Most people exposed to trauma do *not* develop PTSD; social support is protective. ICD-11 also defines **complex PTSD** (with problems in emotion regulation, self-concept and relationships).

steps.title: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
steps.body:
- **Obsessions:** intrusive, unwanted thoughts, images or urges causing anxiety (contamination, harm, symmetry, taboo thoughts)
- **Compulsions:** repetitive behaviours or mental acts to reduce the anxiety (washing, checking, counting, reassurance-seeking)

People usually recognise the thoughts as excessive. The first-line psychological treatment is **exposure and response prevention (ERP)**; SSRIs are also used. OCD is not 'liking things neat'.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Telling an anxious person 'just relax' or offering endless reassurance — reassurance often feeds anxiety cycles.
- Assuming everyone exposed to trauma will be damaged for life; resilience is common.
- Pushing someone to retell trauma details before they are ready. Trauma processing belongs in professional therapy.

steps.title: Try this
steps.body: Build a 'fear ladder' for a mild everyday fear (e.g., speaking in class): list 6 steps from easiest (asking one question) to hardest (a 10-minute talk). Rate each 0–100. Start at the step around 30–40. *For severe anxiety, panic or trauma, work with a qualified professional.*

activity.prompt: Order Mohammed's graded exposure ladder from easiest to hardest.
items: Ask one question in a small tutorial
Speak for 1 minute to two friends
Present 2 minutes to a study group of five
Present 5 minutes in class with notes
Present 10 minutes in class and take questions

quiz.q: GAD requires excessive worry for at least:
quiz.why: Generalised anxiety disorder needs excessive worry on most days for at least 6 months.

quiz.q: Avoidance maintains anxiety mainly through:
quiz.why: Avoiding a feared situation brings relief, which rewards the avoidance. That is negative reinforcement, and it keeps the anxiety going.

quiz.q: The first-line psychological treatment for OCD is:
quiz.why: Exposure and response prevention (ERP), a form of CBT, is the first-line psychological treatment for OCD. The person faces feared triggers without doing the compulsion.

quiz.q: PTSD symptoms must last more than:
quiz.why: PTSD is diagnosed when symptoms last more than one month. Shorter reactions can be acute stress disorder.

scenes.text: Rahul, 20, a top-ranked engineering student in Kota, slowly loses interest in everything — even cricket, which he loved.
He sleeps badly, feels worthless and once tells a friend, 'Everyone would be better off without me.'
His friend Simran doesn't argue or lecture. She asks directly if he's thinking of suicide, listens, and helps him call Tele-MANAS and his family.
With treatment and support over months, Rahul recovers. Depression is treatable; asking about suicide does not plant the idea.

steps.title: Major depressive disorder
steps.body:
DSM-5-TR criteria (simplified): at least **5 of 9 symptoms** for **at least 2 weeks**, including **depressed mood or loss of interest/pleasure (anhedonia)**, causing distress or impairment. Other symptoms: weight/appetite change, sleep change, slowed or agitated movement, fatigue, worthlessness or excessive guilt, poor concentration, recurrent thoughts of death or suicide.

**Persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia):** milder but chronic (≥ 2 years in adults).

Depression is a leading cause of disability worldwide (WHO).

steps.title: Bipolar disorders
steps.body:
- **Bipolar I:** at least one **manic episode** — ≥ 1 week of abnormally elevated or irritable mood and increased energy, with symptoms like decreased need for sleep, grandiosity, racing thoughts, risky behaviour; often severe impairment
- **Bipolar II:** at least one **hypomanic** episode (milder, ≥ 4 days) and at least one major depressive episode

Bipolar disorder is highly heritable; mood stabilisers such as lithium are important treatments. Antidepressants alone can be risky in bipolar disorder, which is why careful assessment matters.

steps.title: Cognitive models of depression
steps.body:
Aaron **Beck's cognitive triad:** negative views of the **self**, the **world** and the **future**, maintained by thinking errors (overgeneralisation, catastrophising, all-or-nothing thinking).

**Learned helplessness** (Seligman) and its reformulation — attributing bad events to internal, stable, global causes — is linked to depression. **Behavioural activation** (scheduling meaningful activities) is an effective treatment component on its own.

steps.title: Suicide: facts and how to help
steps.body:
- Asking someone directly about suicide **does not increase risk**; it often brings relief.
- Warning signs: talking about death or being a burden, hopelessness, withdrawing, giving away possessions, sudden calm after a crisis, increased substance use.
- **How to help:** stay with them, listen without judging, ask directly, remove access to means if safe, connect them to help, and follow up.
- India: **Tele-MANAS 14416** (free, 24×7), **112** for emergencies.

If you yourself are struggling right now, please pause and call 14416 or someone you trust.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- 'Just think positive' — depression is not a choice or a weakness.
- Promising to keep suicidal thoughts secret. Safety comes before secrecy.
- Assuming high achievers can't be depressed.

steps.title: Try this
steps.body: Write down the exact words you would use: 'I care about you. Are you thinking about killing yourself?' Saying it once in private makes it easier to say when it matters.

a.text: A friend texts at night: 'I'm so tired of everything. Nothing will ever get better.' What do you reply?

choices.label: 'Don't be silly, you have so much to live for!'
choices.feedback: Well-meant, but it can feel dismissive.

choices.label: 'I'm here. That sounds really heavy. Are you thinking about ending your life?'
choices.feedback: Direct, caring and opens the door.

b.text: They reply 'ok whatever' and go quiet. What now?

choices.label: Call them, say you're worried, and ask directly about suicide
choices.feedback: Re-engaging is the right move.

choices.label: Leave it till morning
choices.feedback: When someone hints at hopelessness, checking in now matters.

c.text: They say they've been thinking about it. What do you do?

choices.label: Stay with them (in person or on the phone), help them call Tele-MANAS 14416, and involve a trusted adult or family member
choices.feedback: Connecting to help while staying with them is ideal. In immediate danger, call 112.

choices.label: Promise to keep it a secret
choices.feedback: Secrecy can cost a life; safety comes first.

end1.text: Your friend gets support that night and starts treatment. Later they thank you for asking. Remember to look after yourself too.

end2.text: This path risks leaving your friend alone with their thoughts. Review the steps: ask directly, listen, stay, connect to help (14416 / 112), follow up.

quiz.q: Major depression requires symptoms for at least:
quiz.why: Major depression needs symptoms for at least 2 weeks, in DSM-5-TR (low mood or loss of interest plus other symptoms).

quiz.q: Asking someone directly about suicidal thoughts:
options: Puts the idea in their head
Does not increase risk and can help
quiz.why: Research shows that asking someone directly about suicidal thoughts does not plant the idea or raise the risk. It can help them feel heard and open the way to support.

quiz.q: Beck's cognitive triad involves negative views of:
quiz.why: Beck's cognitive triad of depression is a negative view of the self, the world and the future.

quiz.q: A manic episode in Bipolar I lasts at least:
quiz.why: A manic episode (Bipolar I) lasts at least one week. A hypomanic episode is milder and lasts at least 4 days.

story.title: The voices and the village temple

scenes.text: Suresh, 23, from a village near Tumakuru, begins hearing voices commenting on him and believes neighbours are plotting against him.
His family first takes him to a faith healer. Months pass; he worsens.
A district mental health programme team visits, explains schizophrenia, and starts antipsychotic medication and family psychoeducation.
Within a year, Suresh helps on the farm again. His mother now speaks at village meetings about mental illness.

steps.title: Schizophrenia spectrum
steps.body:
**Schizophrenia** involves at least two of: **delusions**, **hallucinations**, **disorganised speech**, grossly disorganised or catatonic behaviour, **negative symptoms** — with at least one of the first three — and continuous signs for at least 6 months (DSM-5-TR).
- **Positive symptoms:** added experiences (hallucinations, delusions)
- **Negative symptoms:** reductions (flat affect, reduced speech, low motivation, social withdrawal)
- **Cognitive symptoms:** attention, working memory and planning difficulties

Onset is typically late adolescence to early adulthood. It is *not* 'split personality' (that is a misconception confused with dissociative identity disorder).

steps.title: Causes
steps.body: Strong heritability, but no single gene; many small-effect genetic variants. Environmental risks include obstetric complications, childhood adversity, urban upbringing, migration, and heavy **cannabis use** in adolescence. The **dopamine hypothesis** (excess dopamine activity in certain pathways linked to positive symptoms) underlies how antipsychotics work, but glutamate and other systems are also implicated. The **stress–vulnerability model** (Zubin & Spring) explains relapses triggered by stress in vulnerable people.

steps.title: Treatments that work
steps.body:
- **Psychotherapies:** **CBT** (Beck, Ellis's related REBT) for depression, anxiety and more; **exposure**-based therapies; **DBT** (Marsha Linehan) for emotion dysregulation and self-harm; interpersonal therapy; family therapy
- **Medication** (prescribed and monitored by psychiatrists): SSRIs and other antidepressants, mood stabilisers (lithium), antipsychotics. Medicines have benefits and side effects; decisions are made with a doctor, never by stopping or starting on your own.
- **Combined** therapy + medication often works best for moderate–severe conditions.
- **Community and task-sharing approaches:** trained lay health workers delivering psychological interventions — e.g., Vikram Patel and colleagues' trials in Goa (Healthy Activity Program for depression) — help close the treatment gap.

steps.title: Stigma and recovery
steps.body:
Stigma delays help-seeking: people fear being labelled 'mad', losing jobs or marriage prospects. Ways to reduce it: contact with people with lived experience, accurate language ('a person with schizophrenia', not 'a schizophrenic'), media that avoids sensationalism.

**Recovery** means living a meaningful life, with or without ongoing symptoms. Many people with serious mental illness work, study and raise families.

steps.title: When to seek professional help
steps.body:
Seek help from a psychiatrist, clinical psychologist or doctor when symptoms last weeks, disrupt study/work/relationships, involve hearing or seeing things others don't, include thoughts of self-harm, or involve heavy substance use. In India: Tele-MANAS **14416**; emergencies **112**; college counselling centres; district hospitals under the District Mental Health Programme.

*This lesson is general education, not medical advice or a diagnosis.*

steps.title: Try this
steps.body: Find your nearest mental-health service (college counsellor, district hospital psychiatry OPD) and save the number in your phone with Tele-MANAS 14416. You may need it for someone else one day.

activity.prompt: Questions people rarely ask aloud about mental illness

items.q: Does seeing a psychiatrist mean I'm 'mad'?
items.a: No. Psychiatrists treat many common conditions like anxiety, depression and sleep problems. Seeing one is like seeing any specialist doctor.

items.q: Will I have to take medicines forever?
items.a: It depends on the condition and the person. Many people take medicine for a defined period. Decisions about starting, changing or stopping are made with your doctor; stopping suddenly can be harmful.

items.q: Is therapy just talking? How does it help?
items.a: Evidence-based therapies like CBT teach specific skills: noticing thinking traps, testing beliefs, gradually facing fears, problem-solving and scheduling meaningful activities.
Professionals keep what you share confidential, with limited exceptions such as serious risk to you or others. You can ask about confidentiality at the start.

items.q: Can people with schizophrenia live normal lives?
items.a: Many do — working, studying, marrying — especially with early treatment, family support and continued care.

quiz.q: Which is a negative symptom of schizophrenia?
quiz.why: Negative symptoms of schizophrenia are reductions in normal functions, such as flat affect and low motivation. Delusions and hallucinations are positive symptoms.

quiz.q: Schizophrenia is the same as 'split personality'.
quiz.why: Schizophrenia is not 'split personality'. That is a common myth. It involves psychosis (hallucinations, delusions, disorganised thinking), whereas dissociative identity disorder involves identity states.

quiz.q: DBT was developed by:
quiz.why: Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT) was developed by Marsha Linehan, originally for borderline personality disorder.

quiz.q: Task-sharing in mental health means:
options: Trained lay health workers deliver some psychological interventions
quiz.why: Task-sharing means trained lay health workers deliver some psychological interventions, which helps close the treatment gap where specialists are few.

questions.q: The 'four Ds' include deviance, distress, dysfunction and:
questions.why: The 'four Ds' of abnormality are deviance, distress, dysfunction and danger (to self or others).

questions.q: Tele-MANAS number in India:
questions.why: Tele-MANAS, India's tele-mental-health service, can be reached on 14416.

questions.q: Panic disorder involves:
options: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks plus worry or avoidance
questions.why: Panic disorder involves recurrent unexpected panic attacks, followed by persistent worry about more attacks or changes in behaviour (avoidance). One attack alone is not enough.

questions.q: Hearing voices others do not is a:
questions.why: Hearing voices that others do not is a hallucination, a perception without an external stimulus. A delusion is a fixed false belief.

questions.q: Exposure therapy works mainly by:
options: Facing feared situations to learn safety without avoidance
questions.why: Exposure therapy has people face feared situations gradually. They learn that the feared outcome does not happen, and the avoidance cycle is broken.

questions.q: Hypomania differs from mania in that it:
options: Is milder and lasts at least 4 days
questions.why: Hypomania is a milder elevated mood than mania, lasting at least 4 days, and is seen in Bipolar II. Mania lasts at least a week and causes marked impairment.

questions.q: Repeated hand-washing to reduce anxiety about germs is a:
questions.why: Repeated hand-washing to reduce anxiety about germs is a compulsion, a behaviour done to neutralise the anxiety from an obsession (the intrusive thought).

questions.q: Section 115 of the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 concerns:
options: Presumption of severe stress in suicide attempts
questions.why: Section 115 of the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 presumes severe stress in a person who attempts suicide, so such a person should receive care and not punishment.

questions.q: Which environmental factor is linked to higher psychosis risk?
questions.why: Heavy cannabis use in adolescence is linked to a higher risk of psychosis later. Diet, exercise and bilingualism are not risk factors.

questions.q: The dopamine hypothesis mainly relates to:
questions.why: The dopamine hypothesis links excess dopamine activity to positive symptoms of schizophrenia, and antipsychotics work by blocking D2 receptors. It explains negative symptoms less well.

questions.q: Complex PTSD is a diagnosis in:
questions.why: Complex PTSD (CPTSD) is a diagnosis in ICD-11, the WHO system. It follows prolonged trauma and includes problems with emotion regulation and relationships.

questions.q: The Healthy Activity Program trial in Goa demonstrated:
options: Lay counsellors can effectively deliver behavioural activation for depression
questions.why: The Healthy Activity Program trial in Goa (Patel et al.) found that lay counsellors can effectively deliver behavioural activation for depression, so task-sharing works.

questions.q: Why might prescribing an antidepressant alone be risky in bipolar disorder?
options: It may trigger mania or mood destabilisation in some patients
questions.why: In bipolar disorder, an antidepressant alone can push some patients into mania or destabilise mood. So assessment is careful, and a mood stabiliser is usually used.
